title: Backend error: compare normalized outcomes
summary: Compare normalized error outcomes with serving latency before treating a degradation as a backend symptom.
prerequisites: A complete observation window is available.
Error-rate and request-outcome evidence use the same replay interval.
diagnostic_checks: Compare the error rate with request outcome counts.
Compare the error window with TTFT and ITL observations.
rollback_criteria: Do not change a live deployment from this evidence.
Return the simulator to its recorded pre-action state if an approved simulation is not verified.
verification_criteria: Re-measure error rate and request outcomes after an approved simulation.
Treat recovery as unverified when normalized outcome evidence is missing or contradictory.

title: Backend slowdown: compare execution signals
summary: Compare ITL, TTFT, and queue observations before treating an execution-interval change as explanatory.
prerequisites: A complete observation window and matching baseline are available.
The serving signals have consistent units and freshness.
diagnostic_checks: Compare ITL with its baseline and with TTFT.
Check whether queue observations corroborate the latency change.
rollback_criteria: Do not change a live deployment from this evidence.
Use the recorded simulator state as the rollback point for an approved simulation.
verification_criteria: Re-measure ITL, TTFT, and queue observations after an approved simulation.
Treat recovery as unverified when the comparison window is incomplete.

title: Capacity queueing: compare waiting pressure
summary: Compare waiting requests, queue wait, and latency with the deployment snapshot before selecting a bounded simulator action.
prerequisites: A complete observation window and matching baseline are available.
Queue and latency observations pass the data-quality checks.
diagnostic_checks: Compare queue depth and queue wait with TTFT and ITL.
Check readiness and revision evidence for the same observation window.
rollback_criteria: Do not change a live deployment or serving system from this evidence.
Use the recorded pre-action replica count as the simulator rollback point.
verification_criteria: Re-measure TTFT, queue depth, queue wait, error rate, ITL, and ready replicas after an approved simulation.
Mark recovery unverified when any required measurement is missing or contradictory.

title: Replica or deployment regression: check readiness state
summary: Check replica readiness, deployment revision, and serving pressure together before treating a replica or deployment change as explanatory.
prerequisites: A complete observation window is available.
The applicable scaling policy and its version are identified.
diagnostic_checks: Compare desired and ready replicas with the serving signals.
Compare the deployment revision with the configuration-change evidence.
rollback_criteria: Do not change a live deployment or autoscaler from this evidence.
For the v1 simulator action, use the recorded pre-action replica count as the rollback point.
verification_criteria: Re-measure ready replicas, revision, and the corroborating serving signal after an approved simulation.
Mark recovery unverified when readiness, revision, or pressure evidence is missing or contradictory.

title: Workload shape change: compare token distributions
summary: Compare input-token distribution and prefill or TTFT observations before treating a workload-shape change as explanatory.
prerequisites: A complete observation window and matching baseline are available.
Token measurements are normalized and contain no prompt content.
diagnostic_checks: Compare input-token percentiles with the baseline distribution.
Compare the token change with prefill and TTFT observations.
rollback_criteria: Do not change a live deployment from this evidence.
Return the simulator to its recorded pre-action state if an approved simulation is not verified.
verification_criteria: Re-measure token distribution, prefill, and TTFT after an approved simulation.
Treat recovery as unverified when workload-shape evidence is incomplete.
